title.narrative: Supporting Sudan in Preventing and combatting the illicit trafficking of cultural property

description.narrative:
The most recent destructive man made hazard to Sudan’s cultural heritage is the outbreak of war on April 15, 2023, between the Sudan Armed Forces (SAF) and the Rapid Support Forces (RSF), and continued till now. Its negative impact on the Sudan’s cultural heritage can be summarized as follows: 1. Destruction of historical monuments in the war zone in Khartoum, Omdurman and Khartoum North. This can be represented by the Republican Palace, the The National Records. 2. Complete destruction of the Natural History Museum as well as the partial destruction of the Sudan National Museum and the Khalifa House Museum. 3. Looting and plundering of major heritage sites on the Tentative List such as Kerma, Sai Island. 4. Encroachment of un authorized urban extensions and agricultural fields towards the World Heritage Properties, Sites on the Tentative List and cultural sites. 5. Impact of big mass of visitors to the World Heritage Prosperities in Gebel Barkal and Island of Meroe. 6. Flourishing of local gold prospection in many un attended cultural sites 7. Flourishing of the illicit trafficking of cultural objects due to security liquidity 8. The consequences of the war on the intangible cultural heritage of Sudan have caused enormous damage, destruction, disruption and distortion to the intangible cultural heritage of various communities in the country as well as impoverishment of living heritage bearers. 9. Social factors that contribute to deterioration processes of the fabric of heritage sites: Religious factors, mass tourism
The work plan aim for the followings:
1. Capacity building for strengthening the capacities of the NCAM staff to deal with the challenges of the damaged antiquities, museums and historical buildings that are affected by the war all over the Sudan. Main required capacity building fields are: a. Damage assessment for the movable and the immovable cultural heritage. b. Approaches to restoration, reconstruction and rehabilitation of the properties and museums, movable and immovable cultural heritage. c. Management plans for the damaged heritage sites and museums. 2. Governance: a. Review of cultural heritage legislation and policy, and disaster management b. Review of the management systems c. Assessment of the human resources available. d. Assessment of fund availability and fund raising e. Coordination with the army, security units, Interpol f. Involvement of NGOs
3. Awareness (II): a. Raising the awareness of Customs officials, security, border police to b. 1954 Convention and its second protocol c. 1970 convention d. With the aim to deal with illicit trafficking of cultural objects through airports and borders.
4. Coordination with international institutions: a. Restitution of stolen objects from museums, libraries and archives. b. Repertoire
